answer: Kin-linking groups agents that share payment rails, vault addresses, or timing patterns into one identity cluster. Each new identity requires staked marble—cryptographic collateral locked per cluster, not per agent. When a prism analysis reveals matching on-chain fingerprints—same funding source, correlated transaction timing, or shared contract calls—the system merges them under a single stake horizon. An attacker spawning a thousand fake agents still holds only one effective vote and one reward allocation, making sybil multiplication economically pointless.
